Fellow Award

This award recognizes members of TMS who are qualified for elevation to the Class of Fellow by reason of outstanding contributions to the practice of metallurgy, materials science, and technology. The award is considered a pinnacle award.

Fellows shall be persons who have been full members of TMS for at least five years continuously and shall be qualified for elevation to the Class of Fellow by reason of outstanding contributions to the practice of minerals, metals, or materials science and technology. Fellows shall be entitled to use the title of "Fellow of The Minerals, Metals & Materials Society." Posthumous nominations for Fellow will not be accepted for consideration by the subcommittee. A nomination is good for three years provided it meets criteria for the award each year. If a nomination is unsuccessful in a three-year cycle, the candidate must wait three years before being renominated.

For more information on this award, the nomination criteria, and the selection criteria, view the bylaws.

How to Nominate

Submission Deadline:April 1 of each year.

Only a member of TMS may nominate a candidate for Fellow.

The nomination package should include:

- Completed Fellow Award nomination form requiring information such as the candidate's employment information, education information, professional accomplishments, evidence of accomplishments, and service to the profession.

- A short CV, no more than 5 pages.

- Three letters of support/recommendation may accompany the nomination package. These letters should be no more than 2 pages in length and focus on additional information/perspectives that complement/augment the nomination form and CV, rather than replicating the information. No more than one of the individuals involved in the nomination, either as nominator or letter writer, may come from the same organization as the nominee. (The completed nomination form acts as the letter of recommendation from the principal nominator; no letter is needed from the principal nominator.)

Send complete nomination packet to TMS Awards.

Please note the following before submitting a nomination:- If a nomination package (CV, letters of recommendation, accomplishments, etc.) is over the limit as specified on the nomination form, the principal nominator will be asked to refine the package, or the package will be rejected.

title: Title: Supplementing Recurrent Neural Networks with Annealing to Solve Combinatorial Optimization Problems
author: Authors Shoummo Ahsan Khandoker; Jawaril Munshad Abedin; Mohamed Hibat-Allah
date: 2022-07-17
---
Condensed Matter > Disordered Systems and Neural Networks

[Submitted on 17 Jul 2022 (v1), last revised 26 Oct 2023 (this version, v2)]

Title:Supplementing Recurrent Neural Networks with Annealing to Solve Combinatorial Optimization Problems

View PDFAbstract:Combinatorial optimization problems can be solved by heuristic algorithms such as simulated annealing (SA) which aims to find the optimal solution within a large search space through thermal fluctuations. The algorithm generates new solutions through Markov-chain Monte Carlo techniques. This sampling scheme can result in severe limitations, such as slow convergence and a tendency to stay within the same local search space at small temperatures. To overcome these shortcomings, we use the variational classical annealing (VCA) framework that combines autoregressive recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with traditional annealing to sample solutions that are uncorrelated. In this paper, we demonstrate the potential of using VCA as an approach to solving real-world optimization problems. We explore VCA's performance in comparison with SA at solving three popular optimization problems: the maximum cut problem (Max-Cut), the nurse scheduling problem (NSP), and the traveling salesman problem (TSP). For all three problems, we find that VCA outperforms SA on average in the asymptotic limit by one or more orders of magnitude in terms of relative error. Interestingly, we reach large system sizes of up to $256$ cities for the TSP. We also conclude that in the best case scenario, VCA can serve as a great alternative when SA fails to find the optimal solution.

1910-1919

1910

- Intermission period between classes changed from five to ten minutes.

- Cosmopolitan Club house damaged by fire.

- Argos Club became chapter of Phi Sigma Kappa fraternity.

- Aztec Club re-organized as Psi Upsilon fraternity.

- Baseball team took Western Conference championship, having won all of its fourteen intercollegiate games.

- Mary E. Fawcett appointed Acting Dean of Women.

- Class of 1910 donated terra cotta container–known as Celebration Urn–which was installed on Illinois Field

- First Homecoming on UI campus occurred. Illinois football team defeated Chicago by a score of 3-0.

1911

- The University of Illinois Alumni Association of India became the first overseas Illini club.

- Control of Daily Illini invested in a board of six trustees–three faculty members and three undergraduates.

- President William Howard Taft visited the University.

- Publication of Facts for Freshmen authorized.

- First Siren published.

1912

- Champaign voted to go alcohol-free.

- Ex-President Theodore Roosevelt visited Champaign.

- Council of Administration ruled that students may not join fraternities until they have completed eleven hours of study.

- First annual mass meeting for women held.

- Pan-Hellenic Council voted against hazing.

- Colleges of Literature and Arts and of Science combined.

- Student votes defeated petition to open theaters on Sundays.

- Chapter of Jewish fraternity Zeta Beta Tau established.

- Robert Zuppke appointed football coach.

- Transportation Building completed.

- Class of 1912 donated "Eternal Flame" bench.

1913

- First issue of Fortnightly Notes, supplement to the Alumni Quarterly, published.

- Lincoln Hall dedicated.

- Kappa Alpha Nu, first African-American fraternity on campus, was organized. Group's name was later changed to Kappa Alpha Psi.

- Ex-President Draper died.

- Phi Beta sorority became Gamma Phi Beta.

- Trustees approved system of freshmen advisers.

- All classes adopted class hats.

- Sack rush replaced pushball contest.

- East wing of Commerce (now Administration) Building completed.

- Council of Administration banned popular dances from University functions.

- Lincoln Hall gateway was gift of Class of 191

Many student branches have hosted SPAx events. Here are descriptions of some events that the organizers have shared with us. Be sure to share your event reports with us, so we can include your event here as well.

St Luke's Karundas Secondary School and Gathungururu Girls High School Mentorship - Dedan Kimathi University of Technology

Read More The event began with a general introductory session where we introduced ourselves and explained our backgrounds and courses. We then divided the students into two groups. Each group participated in a morning mentorship session, discussing topics ranging from academics to general life advice. Many students had questions about university courses, which we answered to the best of our abilities.

In the afternoon, we swapped the groups to provide them with diverse perspectives and ideas. The day concluded with two concurrent sessions: one where interested students explored projects showcased by one of our event partners, and another where students engaged in one-on-one mentoring sessions.

MAGNIFY - Anil Neerukonda Institute of Technology and Sciences

Read More MAGNIFY, held on the 11th and 12th of April 2024 at Anil Neerukonda Institute of Technology and Sciences, was a transformative educational event that empowered students for their professional journey. The event featured dynamic sessions, including a hands-on graphic design workshop by Ms. Joyce Christina, which enriched participants with essential skills and creative insights. A successful IEEE membership drive to bolster the Vizag Bay Section's community of professionals and students also took place. Additionally, Day 2 featured a guest lecture on the basic infrastructure of electric hybrid vehicles, offering an in-depth overview of the foundational components and systems essential to these vehicles, along with a Poster Design Competition that showcased exceptional creativity from the participants.

Prize Items: $5,000 and a certificate for Graduate student; $5,000 and a certificate for the Undergraduate student. Funds will be paid to the school on behalf of the student.

Frequency: Annually

Deadline: 1 December
